summary: Approval, revisions and publishing in own-dashboard 8df25a5 are tight on byte identity and loose on owner time. revisionContentHash is sha256 over the canonical revision minus assets[].url only, so it binds title, caption, format, deck, every rendered asset sha256/MIME/size/alt, account, scheduledAt, sources, knowledgeIds, templateVersion, promptVersion, model and traceId. Approval (marketing_approve_revision) stores approved_hash=content_hash and creates one queued publication; edits, skips, returns, newer source revisions and calendar rebinds all null approved_hash. The publisher recomputes the hash, re-downloads every JPEG and checks sha256, JPEG, 4:5..1.91:1 geometry, declared size, sRGB and 8 MiB before the first container, reads content_publishing_limit, and posts media_publish once behind a durable intent. Weak points: scheduledAt is in the hash and a slot missed by 15 minutes turns the approved revision into failed, so every reschedule or missed slot costs an edit, a synchronous re-render and a new approval; returned and skipped posts can neither be re-approved nor regenerated; a transient error while creating any of up to ten carousel children strands the publication in reconciliation with no owner way out; marketing-assets is never purged and its render-key objects are shared between revisions, so retention needs reference counting. For task G the code supports the 'lazy covers + cache warming' option with fewer changes than the draft model claims: the render-key cache already makes a kit switch an ordinary edit whose render is a cache hit, so no variants table is needed; the deck schema, render key, edit schema and tracer need a kit field. Measured render cost is about 0.82 MB and 0.5-0.7 s per 7-slide deck locally, so five kits are about 4.1 MB and 2.6-3.6 s of CPU, lower than the brief's 6-8 MB and 8-15 s.

facts.fact: The approval identity excludes only assets[].url; any future asset field is covered by default.

Hashed fields (strict schema): schemaVersion, brand, title, caption, format, sources, knowledgeIds, assets{sha256,mimeType,width,height,alt}, account{id,platform,handle}, collaborators?, scheduledAt, timeZone, templateVersion, promptVersion, model, traceId, deck?. The brief's list (2.6) omits title, caption, promptVersion, model, traceId and knowledgeIds.
canonicalJson sorts object keys; arrays keep order, so slide and asset order are part of the hash.

Approval: marketing_approve_revision (authenticated, security definer) checks campaign/entry, content_hash = expected, status review|approved and ready, no blocking render report, deck asset count = slide count, scheduledAt > now(), sources valid, verified account; then sets approved_hash=content_hash and inserts one queued marketing_publications row (unique revision_id, platform).

Return/skip: marketing_decide_revision sets status returned|skipped, nulls approved_at/approved_hash and cancels the queued publication; refused once a publication is claimed, published or in reconciliation.

Supersede: marketing_save_revision with p_replace sets the previous row superseded with approved_hash null and cancels its queued publication; refused when the previous is publishing, published, reconciliation or superseded or has a claimed/published/reconciliation publication.
A newer source revision, a changed content hash or an ineligible source supersedes every review/approved/returned/failed revision citing it.

Owner edit of a deck revision always drops assets and re-renders, even for a caption- or schedule-only change; it saves first (superseding the old revision) and renders synchronously with a 45 s abort inside a 60 s route.
The edit route refuses a schedule in the past or more than 6 days ahead (signed URLs last 7 days).
Render attach may only add assets: the deck, text, account and schedule must stay byte-identical, and a ready attach needs one asset per slide and a non-blocking report.

Publisher gate: status approved|publishing, approved_at valid, approved_hash = content_hash = recomputed hash; ready and readiness; render report; account binding, enabled and verified; MARKETING_PUBLISH_ENABLED and MARKETING_DNESKAI_PUBLISH_ENABLED; API version; token present/unexpired; scopes instagram_business_basic + instagram_business_content_publish; each source unchanged, usable and observed within 15 min; within the 15-min window after scheduledAt; alt present and <= 1000; carousel 2-10; declared 4:5..1.91:1 geometry; <= 30 hashtags and <= 20 mentions.

verifyAssets downloads every asset (approved host, no redirect, 10 s), checks Content-Type, <= 8 MiB, sha256 equals assets[].sha256, then decodes with sharp: JPEG, valid geometry, orientation 1, width/height equal the declared ones, colour space srgb.
Quota: reads content_publishing_limit (quota_usage, config.quota_total) and holds when unavailable or exhausted; no fixed number is assumed.

Carousel: after a durable 'intent:<content hash>' checkpoint, one POST per child (image_url, is_carousel_item, alt_text), one parent POST with media_type CAROUSEL and children, up to 3 status polls at 1 s, revalidation of the whole gate, a durable publish-intent checkpoint, then exactly one media_publish POST and a permalink read.
Collaborators go on the parent container only when the revision records them; no DNESKAi code path writes collaborators.

Expired claim leases become reconciliation ('lease-expired'); approved revisions whose queued publication is more than 15 min past its slot become failed and lose approved_hash; their publications fail with publish-window-expired.
Receipt: marketing_finish_publication writes status, container id, media id, permalink and error code; receipts are typed per state (queued, claimed, published, failed, reconciliation, cancelled).
Token: long-lived Instagram tokens last 60 days; the scheduler refreshes when fewer than 10 days remain and the token is at least 24 h old; a stored DB token wins over the env bootstrap.

Signed URLs: renewed by the daily tick when they expire within 48 h, for up to 50 newest review/approved revisions; renewal re-hashes the stored bytes, and SQL accepts only a changed signature on the same object path; content_hash and approved_hash stay.
Rendered slides are cached per render key at <owner>/marketing/dneskai/slides/<renderKey>.jpg, so one object can serve several revisions.
Only marketing-media (source photos) has a purge; nothing deletes marketing-assets objects.

findings.title: scheduledAt is inside the approval hash, so every reschedule and every missed slot needs an edit, a re-render and a new approval
findings.claim: The hash covers scheduledAt (and account). Moving a post by a minute creates a new revision, supersedes the approved one, re-renders the deck synchronously and needs a new approval. Approval is also refused once scheduledAt has passed, so a post not approved before its slot cannot be approved at all without an edit. Approved posts more than 15 min past their slot are turned into failed with approved_hash cleared; nothing moves them to the next free slot.

impact.statement: Each missed 08:00 slot costs the owner two round trips and an approval; the brief's 'auto-move to the next free slot' cannot exist without re-approval under today's hash.
impact.reason: A missed slot or a time change costs the owner an edit, a re-render wait and a second approval every time, which directly fights the 10-minute target.
impact.ownerDecision: Decide whether the publish time may change after approval without a new approval (time outside the hash, or an auto-move to the next free slot), or stay strictly bound.

findings.recommendation: Owner decision: split the identity into a content hash (bytes, text, deck, account) that approval binds and a schedule the owner may shift within a rule (for example: same day, to the next free slot, never earlier than now + 5 min) without re-approval, recorded as an event. The hard rule binds pixels and text, which stays intact. If the owner keeps time in the hash, at least skip the re-render for caption/schedule-only edits and offer 'move to next free slot' as a one-click edit+approve.

findings.title: A transient error while creating any carousel child strands the publication in reconciliation with no owner path out
findings.claim: The durable 'intent:<hash>' checkpoint is written before the first child POST, and every failure after it becomes reconciliation. Reconciliation of an intent container (not a numeric id) returns container-identity-unavailable forever. Child containers are unpublished and expire on Meta's side, so recreating them would not publish twice, but the code applies the single-POST rule to container creation too. A revision in reconciliation cannot be edited, returned or skipped (SQL refuses), so the post is frozen.

findings.title: Variant model draft overstates render cost and storage per post
findings.claim: The draft variant model estimates 7-15 s warm and about 9 MB for five 7-slide kits (brief: 8-15 s, 6-8 MB). The measured 7-slide deck is 820 KB and 0.50-0.52 s warm (0.72 s cold) on an M2, so five kits are about 4.1 MB and 2.6-3.6 s plus uploads. Vercel CPU is slower and storage uploads add round trips, but the job budget is not the binding constraint the draft assumes.

evidence.excerpt: 5 × deck (≈ 7–15 s warm for 7 slides, more when cold) ... ≈ 5 × 7 × 250 KB ≈ 9 MB

impact.statement: Changes the recommendation's justification: pre-rendering all kits fits the job, the open costs are uploads, storage and never-chosen kits.
impact.reason: The measured numbers make pre-rendering five kits look cheap, which changes the task-G decision.

findings.recommendation: Measure one five-kit render with uploads on a Vercel preview (or the worker) before choosing between eager and lazy; until then use 4 MB and ~3 s CPU as the planning figure, labelled estimate.

truth.evidence: variant-approval-model.md:11 says 7-15 s and ~9 MB; measurements/bench-render-run1.json passes: cold 720.5 ms, warm 503.8-521.7 ms, 820,252 JPEG bytes for 7 slides on an Apple M2. Five kits x that = ~4.1 MB, ~2.5-3.6 s, an extrapolation since the other kits do not exist; uploads and Vercel CPU are excluded.

findings.title: Approval and publish gates are strong and tested; keep them unchanged under the Design Lab
findings.claim: Exact-bytes approval is enforced three times: SQL approve compares content_hash, claim_due requires approved_hash = content_hash and ready, and the publisher recomputes the hash, re-downloads every asset and compares sha256, geometry and sRGB before any container, then revalidates the whole gate after the container is FINISHED and before media_publish. 87 tests cover identity, renewal, edits, media database and the publisher.

findings.title: The publication window is 15 minutes and ticks run every 5 minutes, and a live publish needs 30 s of tick budget; a busy tick can lose the slot
findings.claim: A queued publication is claimable only between scheduledAt and +15 min; ticks every 5 min give three chances. A live publish starts only with 30 s of the soft budget left; the scheduler yields other categories when a publication is due within 5 min, which mitigates this. If all three ticks hold (credential, quota or a slow first category), the revision becomes failed with approval cleared (approval-01).

evidence.excerpt: p.status='queued' and p.scheduled_at<=now() and p.scheduled_at>=now()-interval '15 minutes'

impact.statement: Unmeasured until live; with the yield rule the risk looks low, but a miss needs owner re-approval.
impact.reason: The scheduler already yields to publishing and approval-01 covers missed slots; the residual risk is small.

findings.recommendation: Keep the window; record held codes per publication in the review UI and send a notification when a publication ends publish-window-expired. Revisit with production tick durations (production map).

truth.evidence: control_surface.sql:236 claim window scheduled_at..+15 min; scheduler.ts:63 yield 5 min used at :246; scheduler.ts:69 30 s minimum start used at :367.

options.option: 1 Pre-render all five kits in the generation job
options.fitToCode: Possible: the job renders the deck already; adding 4 more decks costs ~2-3 s CPU locally and 28 more uploads; storage ~4 MB/post. Alternatives would sit only in the render cache (no table needed).
options.verdict: viable but renders kits never chosen

options.option: 2 Lazy: covers for all kits first, full decks on demand, warmed by a tick unit
options.fitToCode: Best fit: render cache by key means warming and on-demand renders never duplicate work; a switch is an edit that hits the cache.

options.option: 3 Store alternatives outside revision.assets and write the chosen kit into the deck at approval
options.fitToCode: Conflicts with marketing_attach_revision_render (only assets may change after save) and with approve comparing a stored content_hash; the hash would have to be computed at approval.
